nodes.label: Skill Creator
nodes.rationale: Defines a standard SKILL.md template (frontmatter, Core Workflow, Output Checklist) so that all skills in the collection follow a consistent, discoverable structure.

nodes.label: TypeScript Strict Migrator
nodes.rationale: Recommends incremental, one-flag-at-a-time adoption of strict mode instead of a single switch, so teams can fix errors in manageable phases without blocking development.

nodes.label: Design-to-Component Translator
nodes.rationale: Maps design values to design tokens rather than hardcoded values so components stay consistent with the design system and are easier to retheme.

nodes.label: Frontend Refactor Planner
nodes.rationale: Prioritizes refactor phases by risk (high-traffic pages first) and recommends adding tests before refactoring to mitigate the risk of regressions in legacy code.

nodes.label: Modal & Drawer System Generator
nodes.rationale: Renders modals/drawers via a DOM portal outside the normal component hierarchy so they escape parent overflow/z-index clipping, and traps focus with scroll lock for accessibility.

nodes.label: React Server Components
nodes.rationale: Defaults to Server Components and only opts into 'use client' when interactivity is required, because server components send zero JS to the browser and keep large dependencies off the client bundle.

nodes.label: nodesDS (vis.DataSet)
nodes.rationale: Nodes are seeded with Fermat/golden-angle spiral positions before physics runs, because avoidOverlap would otherwise compute near-zero-distance repulsion that blows the BarnesHut recursion into a stack overflow on large graphs; physics still settles small graphs identically.

nodes.label: Animation & Micro-interaction Pack
nodes.rationale: Recommends animating only transform/opacity and respecting prefers-reduced-motion for performance and accessibility reasons.

nodes.label: Dark Mode Implementer
nodes.rationale: Injects an inline script that applies the resolved theme class before React hydrates, specifically to prevent a flash of the wrong theme (FOUC) on initial load.

nodes.label: Framer Motion Animator
nodes.rationale: Prefers spring physics over tween transitions because springs feel more natural for UI motion, and restricts animation to GPU-accelerated properties (opacity/transform) for performance.

nodes.label: Responsive Design System
nodes.rationale: Uses clamp()-based fluid typography/spacing instead of fixed breakpoint jumps so text and spacing scale smoothly across viewport sizes.

nodes.label: afterDrawing hyperedge renderer
nodes.rationale: The perimeter must follow hull order, not the raw h.nodes order: tracing members in their original order self-intersects whenever the layout doesn't place them in angular order, filling as crossed wedges.

nodes.label: convexHull()
nodes.rationale: Implements Andrew's monotone chain and returns the hull in counter-clockwise order because the perimeter must be traced that way; collinear and duplicate points collapse to the extremes so degenerate member sets render as a segment rather than a zero-area crossed path.

nodes.label: esc()
nodes.rationale: HTML-escape helper — prevents XSS when injecting graph data into innerHTML.

nodes.label: focusNode()
nodes.rationale: Neighbor links use a data-nid attribute plus a delegated click listener instead of inline onclick, because a node id/label sourced from a scraped document or URL can contain a double-quote — unescaped, that both breaks the link and lets a hostile source inject an event handler into the report (stored XSS, #1838).

nodes.label: Form Wizard Builder
nodes.rationale: Validates per-step rather than only at final submission so users get feedback before investing time in later steps.

nodes.label: State & UX Flow Builder
nodes.rationale: Prefers skeleton loaders over spinners and mandates handling all four states (loading/error/empty/success) to avoid inconsistent or broken UI during data fetching.

nodes.label: taste-skill v2 (experimental) / design-taste-frontend
nodes.rationale: Pre-v2, the original taste-skill set the right direction but was easy for agents to skim past; production testing showed recurring 'AI Tells' (em-dash everywhere, section-number eyebrows, decorative dots, fake styled-div screenshots, broken GSAP triggers). v2 closes those gaps with hard rules, canonical code skeletons, and a mandatory pre-flight checklist.

nodes.label: Industrial Brutalism & Tactical Telemetry UI Skill
nodes.norm_label: industrial brutalism & tactical telemetry ui skill
nodes.rationale: Deliberately discards conventional consumer UI patterns to project raw functionality and mechanical precision, borrowing from Swiss print and military HUD conventions.

nodes.label: GPT-Taste Elite UX/GSAP Motion Skill
nodes.rationale: Uses simulated Python RNG seeded by prompt character count to force layout variety, explicitly to break the LLM's statistical bias toward repeating the same first-choice layout.

nodes.label: Image-to-Code Website Design Skill
nodes.rationale: Mandates generating the design image first and analyzing it before coding, because standard AI output collapses into repetitive layout defaults when designed directly in code.

nodes.label: Web Frontend Image-Generation Skill
nodes.rationale: Mandates one horizontal image per page section because compressing multiple sections into a single image makes text, spacing, and buttons too small to analyze or implement faithfully.

nodes.label: Premium Utilitarian Minimalism UI Skill
nodes.rationale: Enforces a list of banned generic defaults (Inter font, Lucide icons, heavy shadows, gradients) specifically to reject standard generic SaaS design trends.

nodes.label: Full-Output Enforcement Skill
nodes.rationale: Built to override default LLM truncation behavior by banning placeholder patterns and brevity-signaling prose, treating any partial output as a broken output.

nodes.label: Redesign Existing Projects Skill
nodes.rationale: Explicitly works within the existing stack rather than rewriting from scratch, to avoid breaking functionality and keep changes reviewable and low-risk.

nodes.label: Compounding Error Avoidance (Truncation as Risk Mitigation)
nodes.norm_label: compounding error avoidance (truncation as risk mitigation)

nodes.label: RLHF and Compute Economics
nodes.rationale: Argues brevity is economically incentivized: exhaustive multi-step reasoning at scale would exceed per-token compute budgets, so RLHF trains models toward short, confident summaries over rigorous solutions.

nodes.label: High-End Visual Design (soft-skill)
nodes.rationale: Encodes a 'Variance Mandate' so the agent never repeats the same layout/aesthetic twice, while staying inside a fixed 'Apple-esque / Linear-tier' language; Double-Bezel nested-container pattern exists so cards read as machined physical hardware rather than flat divs.

nodes.label: Design System: Taste Standard (DESIGN.md)
nodes.rationale: Configuration dials (Creativity 8, Density 4, Variance 8, Motion 6) are set deliberately above the symmetric/predictable baseline specifically to prevent 'symmetrical boredom' while keeping motion restrained rather than theatrical, per the stated atmosphere goal of feeling 'expensive, intentional, alive'.

nodes.label: Stitch Design Taste Skill
nodes.rationale: Generates DESIGN.md files as the single source of truth for prompting Google Stitch, because Stitch interprets design through natural-language 'Visual Descriptions' rather than code, so the anti-slop directives had to be translated into descriptive prose with precise values.

nodes.label: Design Taste Frontend Skill (v2, taste-skill)
nodes.rationale: Em-dash ban is made binary ('zero em-dashes') rather than 'use sparingly' because the agent historically ignored soft limits; eyebrow-label frequency is capped because every AI-built site places an eyebrow above every section, producing templated rhythm; the beige+brass+espresso premium-consumer palette is banned by default because every premium-consumer AI output reused it, making brands indistinguishable; serif fonts (Fraunces, Instrument Serif) are banned as defaults because 'creative brief = serif' is flagged as the most-tested AI tell in production rounds.

nodes.label: Design Taste Frontend Skill (v1, taste-skill-v1)
nodes.rationale: Preserved unchanged and kept installable under its own name specifically so existing projects depending on its exact behavior are not broken by the substantial v2 rewrite.
